title: Aerosol measurement in children with SARS-CoV-2 and other respiratory infections - Determination of aerosol particle count and aerosol particle size distribution in the exhaled air of healthy children and children with respiratory infections, especially children with and after SARS-CoV2 infection
summary:
Aerosols are tiny particles that float in the air. They consist of small droplets and can contain viruses. Larger droplets sink quickly to the ground, but smaller ones remain in the air longer. This is particularly important in closed, poorly ventilated rooms—for example, when breathing, speaking, coughing, or sneezing.
During the coronavirus pandemic (SARS-CoV-2), it has been shown that the virus can also spread via such aerosols. Studies have shown that children emit fewer aerosols than adults when breathing calmly, speaking, or singing.
This study will now investigate how many particles children release into the air when they exhale—and whether viruses can be detected in them. To this end, 150 children aged 2 to 17 with respiratory infections (e.g., coronavirus, RSV, influenza, colds), other gastrointestinal infections, or no infections at all will be examined. The measurements will be taken in doctors' offices and hospitals using a special device called a “Resp-Aer-Meter.”(Fa PALAS, Karlsruhe)
The aim of this study is to find out how well viruses can be detected in exhaled air compared to nasal swabs (PCR test). In cases of gastrointestinal infections, a stool sample will also be examined. In addition, family members will also be tested in 50 cases. The researchers hope this will give them a better understanding of how infections spread within a family.
conditions: Acute upper respiratory infections of multiple and unspecified sites
Viral and other specified intestinal infections

interventions.name: Measurement of aerosol particle size distribution in exhaled air and infection status in children aged 2–17 years with symptoms of respiratory infection or gastroenteritis
Measurement of aerosol particle size distribution in exhaled air and infection status in asymptomatic children aged 2–17 years

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Intervention group:
- Acute respiratory infection
- Acute SARS-CoV-2 infection
- Acute gastroenteritis
Control group
- No symptoms of respiratory and/or gastrointestinal infection
Exclusion criteria:
- Age < 2 years and > 17 years
- Lack of consent from legal guardians or the participant
- Chronic pre-existing cardiac, pulmonary, or allergic conditions
- Malformations of the upper respiratory tract
- Long-term medication (e.g., salbutamol, inhaled steroids)
